summary.headline: Afcons Q2 FY27 revenue fell 6.3% to INR 2,906 crore and PAT to INR 41 crore; management guides FY28 revenue growth of 20-25% but has withheld FY27 guidance.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 2,906 crore, down 6.3% YoY, with EBITDA of INR 316 crore (10.9% margin) and PAT of INR 41 crore versus INR 105 crore a year ago. H1 revenue fell 13.6% YoY to INR 5,633 crore, with H1 PAT at INR 71 crore. Management attributed the weakness to work-front availability, monsoon seasonality, stretched client payments (notably UP Jal Jeevan Mission) and a new ECL provisioning matrix plus one-off provisions for arbitration receivables and a Middle East subsidiary. Order book stands at about INR 43,836 crore excluding L1 orders, with FY27 inflow of about INR 19,437 crore booked so far against a INR 30,000 crore target.

segments.commentary: Identified pending pipeline of about INR 80,000 crore for rest of FY27: hydro about 35%, marine about 35%, surface (road and rail) about 10%, urban infrastructure about 20%.

segments.commentary: Total pipeline of about INR 3.6 lakh crore; 65% domestic and 35% international, split across hydro and underground 20%, marine and industrial 27%, surface and transport 20%, urban infrastructure 32%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order inflow guidance of INR 30,000 crore maintained; management says it is confident of achieving it and beyond.
No FY27 revenue or margin guidance; management held it back due to geopolitical uncertainty and will reinstate once uncertainty eases.
FY28 revenue growth of about 20-25% expected, measured from FY26 base (March 2026), per management clarification.
H2 FY27 execution expected to be stronger than H1; management says H2 revenue will be higher than H1 revenue of INR 5,633 crore.
FY27 capex unchanged at about INR 700 crore and FY28 capex about INR 650 crore.
FY27 year-end gross debt about INR 3,500 crore and net debt about INR 2,750-2,800 crore.
Finance cost run rate (about INR 136 crore per quarter ex bank charges) not expected to rise materially; BG commission could rise if BG utilisation increases.
Other income run rate of about INR 60-70 crore per quarter expected to continue excluding arbitration income.
Expects significant H2 cash flow from operations improvement from mobilisation advances on new orders (Q3-Q4) and recovery of stuck receivables.
capex_capacity: Two tunnel boring machines at Mumbai-Ahmedabad HSR: first TBM in regular operation after initial drive; second TBM initial drive expected to complete in November 2026; management says it is on track for budgeted HSR numbers this year.
Tunnelling turnover expected to ramp from November; depreciation may rise from INR 85-90 crore per quarter toward INR 120-130 crore after Q3, per management agreement.
Greater Male Connectivity: final segment of Thilamale Bridge completed in Q2.
Mithapur-Sipara Elevated Corridor Phase II inaugurated in Bihar during the quarter.
Vadhavan Port: geotechnical work started; work at scale constrained until approach roads are handed over; alternative execution methods under discussion with clients.
demand_pricing: Order intake of about INR 16,000 crore in H1 FY27; FY27 intake to date about INR 19,437 crore excluding L1 orders.
Pending order book above INR 47,000 crore per CFO; INR 43,836 crore per MD at H1-end, both excluding L1.
Croatia order (about INR 7,500 crore) was the only major win carried over from last year; revenue from this project expected to start in FY28. Escalation beyond 10% is compensable; 10% provisioned.
Pune Ring Road tender expected to be awarded in Q4 FY27; Brahmaputra tunnel tenders are out and Afcons expects to be L1.
Competition intense in certain segments; award pace uneven. Domestic bids remain on L1 basis, with first QCBS projects only starting to come.
Pricing and margin: management says gross margin on incremental revenue about 35%; breakeven revenue quoted at about INR 2,400-2,500 crore per quarter.
risks_watch: Collections: client payments stretched across projects; UP Jal Jeevan Mission receivables INR 372 crore outstanding and pending order book INR 474 crore; release tied to 75% completion thresholds.
Contract assets (unbilled) about INR 8,200 crore (INR 6,200 crore current, INR 2,000 crore non-current); management aims to reduce by year end.

Provisioning: new ECL matrix, arbitration-receivable discount provision, and Middle East subsidiary provision; the Q2 ECL quantum was not disclosed (analyst cited about INR 86 crore as a floor). Management says no further provisioning is needed, but a reversal is possible if collections come through.
Arbitration income (INR 183 crore in Q2 per analyst) is uncertain and timing unclear.
Tax rate about 46% of PBT in Q2 due to loss-making overseas subsidiaries (Bangladesh turnover tax) and a 25% rate on Afcons-only profit.
Geopolitical West Asia tensions affecting logistics, input costs and energy availability (including Bangladesh).
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth and order inflow, but cautious and evasive on near-term numbers: no FY27 revenue or margin guidance, and vague on collection timing and the Q2 ECL quantum. Management repeatedly points to H2 improvement without quantifying it.
key_quotes: Not everything has moved at the same pace. Liquidity and collection remain challenging, and execution on the Jal Jeevan Mission project in U.P. continues to remain gradual.
Next year, as we conveyed to you earlier also, we do expect about 20%-25% growth from that of current year, number one.
So, we don't foresee any issue on profitability. Revenue will start in FY '28.
Uncertainty around the economic activity because of war, geopolitical, and related stuff continues, so we have held back any guidance in terms of growth for the time being.

qa_highlights.question: Is H2 FY27 revenue going to be materially higher than H1, or only a smaller YoY decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 revenue will definitely be higher than H1 revenue of INR 5,633 crore, and gave no quantified figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue outlook for FY28 and the High-Speed Rail execution?
qa_highlights.answer: FY28 revenue expected to grow about 20-25% from the current year base. Both TBMs are in operation: first TBM past initial drive and in regular working; second TBM initial drive expected to complete in November, and the company is on track for budgeted HSR numbers this year.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in the ECL provisioning this quarter, given that ECL is normally bucket-based?
qa_highlights.answer: From March 2026 the company moved to a new ECL matrix with automatic provisioning as receivables age across buckets (six months, one year, two years), replacing past-experience-based provisioning. Management said its provisioning is higher than peers; a task force is tracking about 15 stuck projects; arbitration receivables were provided at the company's own initiative for negotiation headroom.

qa_highlights.question: Why not give FY27 or H2 guidance, and what is the implied H2 revenue, given that FY28 growth guidance is given?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance was held back due to geopolitical uncertainty (energy availability in places like Bangladesh, overseas logistics) and will be reinstated when that uncertainty eases. The 20-25% FY28 growth is measured from the March 2026 base. No H2 revenue number was given.

qa_highlights.question: What was the Q2 ECL provision amount and what drove the margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give the Q2 ECL quantum on the call and said it is higher than the INR 86 crore cited by the analyst; it will follow up offline. Breakeven is about INR 2,400-2,500 crore quarterly revenue, and incremental revenue earns about 35% gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further provisioning, and what is the outstanding and stuck receivable position (UP JJM, contract assets)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no further provisioning is expected, with possible reversals if collections come through. UP Jal Jeevan Mission outstanding is INR 372 crore and pending UP order book is INR 474 crore, with release tied to 75% completion. Contract assets (unbilled) stand at about INR 8,200 crore, and the company aims to reduce them by year end.
